key_insight: Encoder-decoder operator learning can be analyzed in a resolution-independent way by passing to a limiting kernel, so approximation, regularization, and optimization effects can be separated cleanly.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical error guarantees for neural operator models built from finite-resolution data, including wide encoder-decoder networks and common bases such as Fourier, wavelets, PCA, and point sampling.
method: Derive an induced operator-valued kernel from a matrix-valued kernel on the encoded space.
Prove convergence of these kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of the associated integral operators.
Analyze regularized SGD and limiting NTK dynamics to obtain upper and lower error bounds, including finite-width effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical upper and lower error bounds, plus polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees when encoding errors decay algebraically.
watch_item: The guarantees rely on asymptotic kernel convergence and encoding error decay, so finite-resolution implementations may deviate if the encoding is too coarse or the width is not sufficiently large.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
